On June 27, 2019, the Michigan Attorney General fled suit in Michigan state court seeking to halt Enbridge's operation of Line 5 by having the 1953 easement declared void and Enbridge's continuing operations declared unlawful. Enbridge was served with the complaint on July 12, 2019. Rather than removing the case to fed- eral court within the 30-day deadline required by 28 U. S. C. § 1446(b)(1), Enbridge litigated in state court for months. entry.title: Kathleen M. Barron v. John D. Barron
entry.content:

Panel: STANFILL, C.J., and LAWRENCE, DOUGLAS, and TAUB, JJ., and HORTON, A.R.J.
KATHLEEN M. BARRON
v.
JOHN D. BARRON
TAUB, J. [¶1] John D. Barron appeals from a divorce judgment issued by the District Court (Bangor, Roberts, A.R.J. ) dissolving his marriage to Kathleen M. Barron. John contends that the court erred in distributing marital property because it used information from Kathleen’s 2022 financial statement instead of information from her 2024 financial statement. 1 We agree, vacate the judgment in part, and remand for further proceedings. We also deny Kathleen’s motion for sanctions, which argues that John’s appeal is frivolous.
1 Because the parties share the same surname, we refer to them by their given names. 2 I. BACKGROUND [¶2] Kathleen filed for divorce from John in 2022. In 2022, both Kathleen and John filed financial statements as required by M.R. Civ. P. 108(c). On May 15, 2024, prior to the final hearing on May 31, 2024, Kathleen filed an updated financial statement as required by M.R. Civ. P. 108(d)(4). John did not file an updated financial statement. [¶3] At the final hearing, the only issue s were spousal support and the division of marital property. Kathleen entered her 2024 financial statement in evidence and testified as to its contents. Kathleen also entered John’s 2022 financial statement in evidence. Neither Kathleen’s 2022 financial statement nor an updated financial statement from John were entered in evidence. Title 5 License Maintenance Case

Aug 11, 2026

Providers whose license is under a Title 5 review may use your Title 5 notice to extend your enrollment with MaineCare in MIHMS by six months, and for every six months thereafter, until the Title 5 review is resolved. Providers must complete this update by submitting a maintenance case via the Health PAS Online Portal. They can use the Provider Maintenance User Guide for step-by-step instructions.

Select the “Title 5 License Extension” from the licensing board drop-down menu and complete the maintenance case as usual. Providers can use the ALMS website to search for your license and must take a screenshot to upload with the maintenance case to show the Title 5 status. 

Please ensure the "Term Date” is 6 months after the license expiration date. For example, if you submit your Title 5 review and your license ends on January 30, 2026, extend the “Term Date” out to July 30, 2026. As necessary, repeat this process every six months until the license is renewed. Once the license is renewed, submit another case with the new term date of the license. 

Providers take note of your license expiration dates and plan to submit a maintenance case to update that license information a minimum of 30 days prior to the license expiration date. Be sure to account for this when planning and submitting other maintenance cases.

Note: MaineCare will not reimburse providers for services rendered when they fail to renew and update your license within a maintenance case prior to its expiration.

For questions about this process, please contact Provider Enrollment at 1 (866) 690-5585 option 2.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE: August 12, 2026

Title IV Postsecondary Institutions: Workforce Pell Program Application Now Open

MAINE- The State Workforce Development Board (SWDB) - https://www.maine.gov/swb/board/index.shtml announced the launch of Maine's Workforce Pell Application - https://www.worksourcemaine.com/pages/workforce-pell , providing eligible Title IV postsecondary institutions with an online process to seek approval to offer Workforce Pell-eligible programs.

The launch of the application follows the U.S. Department of Education's publication of the final Workforce Pell regulations - https://www.ed.gov/about/news/press-release/us-department-of-education-issues-final-rule-create-new-workforce-pell-grant-program (effective July 20, 2026). Workforce Pell expands federal Pell Grant eligibility to approved short-term workforce training programs that prepare students for high-skill, high-wage, and in-demand careers. Under Workforce Pell, states are responsible for reviewing and certifying eligible programs before approval by the U.S. Department of Education.

"Workforce Pell opens the door to new education and career opportunities for more people across our state," said Vaughan Woodruff, Chair, State Workforce Development Board. "The Maine Workforce Pell program makes it easier for individuals to access those opportunities, strengthening the futures of Maine workers and Maine's businesses."

On July 30, the SWDB approved the Maine Workforce Pell Program Determination Policy - https://www.worksourcemaine.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/final-workforce-pell-determination-policy-8.11.2026.pdf , establishing the state's process for identifying, reviewing, and recommending eligible short-term workforce training programs for Workforce Pell. Developed in partnership with the Maine Department of Labor, Maine Department of Education, Finance Authority of Maine, Maine Community College System, and University of Maine System, the policy is designed to align eligible programs with high-skill, high-wage, in-demand occupations; ensure quality outcomes for students; and provide a transparent and consistent process for institutions and learners.

"Workforce Pell is an important step toward building a stronger workforce and expanding opportunities for people to gain the skills they need to succeed," said Laura Fortman, Commissioner of the Maine Department of Labor. "By aligning short-term training with the skills Maine employers need, these programs will create pathways to good jobs and help businesses find qualified workers. The State Workforce Development Board's clear, transparent process will ensure training prepares people for in-demand careers while meeting the needs of Maine's economy."

entry.content:
Important Information Regarding Cancellation of Certificate of Title:

Pursuant to Title 29-A, section §669, beginning on July 29, 2026, residents of the state of Maine are able to request cancellation of their Certificate of Title for Tiny Home or Manufactured Home for purposes of obtaining residential real property.

If you are interested in the process of cancelling your current Certificate of Title, check out some of the links below before continuing.

This webpage provides general information about Tiny Homes and Manufactured Homes, with a focus on the titling process requirements and related regulations, as well as the cancellation of Certificate of Title for purposes of obtaining residential real property. It is designed to help homeowners, buyers, sellers, and the public better understand how Tiny Homes and Manufactured Homes are classified, when a title is required, and the processes involved in obtaining, transferring, or updating a title. The information presented is intended as an educational resource based on Maine's applicable guidelines and requirements. Visitors can explore common questions, learn about titling procedures, and find helpful explanations to better navigate the ownership and registration process for Tiny Homes and Manufactured Homes in Maine.

Here are some quick reference links, you may need these before continuing:

Conversion to Real Property Process

Maine State Revised Statues Website 

Property Definitions 

This section provides information to help homeowners, buyers, and other interested parties understand the types of construction, material, and installation that classify each type of home. By outlining these definitions. Read through the below definitions for the appropriate boxes to get more information.

Tiny Home Definition

Pursuant to Maine Statute 29-A, section §101, subsection 80-C, Maine's definition of a "Tiny Home" is a living space permanently constructed on a frame or chassis and designed for use as permanent living quarters that: 

  • Complies with American National Standards Institute standard A 119.5 on plumbing, propane, fire and life safety and construction or National Fire Protection Association standard 1192 on plumbing, propane and fire and life safety for recreational vehicles; 
  • Does not exceed 400 sq. feet in size; 
  • Does not exceed any dimension allowed for operation on a public way; 

  • Is a vehicle without motive power. 

Manufactured Home Definition

Pursuant to Maine Statute 29-A, section §101, subsection 32-B, Maine's definition of a "Manufactured Home" is a structural unit or units designed to be used as a dwelling or dwellings and constructed in a manufacturing facility and then transported by the use of its own chassis or placement on an independent chassis to a building site. 

"Manufactured housing" includes any type of building that is constructed at a manufacturing facility and then transported to a building site where it is used for housing and that may be purchased, sold, offered for sale or brokered by a licensee in the interim. Three types of manufactured housing are included: 

  • Units constructed after June 15, 1976; 
  • State-certified modular homes; 
  • Units constructed prior to June 15, 1976

How to Title your Tiny Home or Manufactured Home

A Certificate of Title establishes legal ownership of a Tiny Home or Manufactured Home in the State of Maine. The application process varies depending on whether the home is new or used and the year of the model. Beginning in 2009, The Bureau of Motor Vehicles began issuing titles for Manufactured Homes and in 2019, the Bureau of Motor Vehicles began issuing titles for Tiny Homes. 

Note: If the manufactured homeowner is deceased, additional documentation may be required depending on the circumstances. Please contact the Bureau of Motor Vehicles, before submitting your application.

1. Determine if the model year is eligible for a Certificate of Title

The following information regarding the home’s year and housing status will help determine which model years are eligible for a Certificate of Title.

  • Manufactured Home: The Secretary of State may issue a Certificate of Title for new or used manufactured housing that was previously issued a State of Maine Certificate of Title, or a model year 2007-or-later model that was never issued a Certificate of Title. 
     
  • Tiny Home: The Secretary of State shall issue certificates of title for new tiny homes beginning with model year 2020. The Secretary of State shall issue a Certificate of Title for a used tiny home of any model year that was previously issued a State of Maine Certificate of Title.
     
2. Identify who must apply for a Certificate of Title and what documents are required

There are generally four categories of individuals who may submit an application for a Certificate of Title. The submission process and required documentation may vary depending on whether the application is completed by the customer or the retail seller/dealer. Please refer to the document list below:

New home purchased from a Maine dealer: The retail seller submits the following:

entry.title: Cancellation of Certificate of Title for Tiny Home and Manufactured Home
entry.content:
Important Information Regarding Cancellation of Certificate of Title:

Pursuant to Title 29-A, section §669, beginning on July 29, 2026, residents of the state of Maine are able to request cancellation of their Certificate of Title for Tiny Home or Manufactured Home for purposes of obtaining residential real property.


When a Tiny Home or Manufactured Home is permanently affixed to land that you own, or land where you have permission from the land owner via a signed sworn statement, you may request to cancel the Certificate of Title. Once the Certificate of Title is cancelled, the home becomes part of the residential real property instead of being treated as personal property. Under Maine law, this process is handled through the county Registry of Deeds and the Maine Secretary of State Bureau of Motor Vehicles.
 

How to Cancel your Certificate of Tittle for Tiny Home or Manufactured Home 

Before requesting cancellation of the title, make sure:

  • You own the Tiny Home or Manufactured Home and the land where it is located; and/or
  • The individual that owns the property has given a sworn signed statement of authorization.
  • The home has been permanently affixed to the property in accordance with Maine law.
  • Any existing liens have been released or the lienholder has agreed to release the lien upon cancellation of the title.

  • This process is not for double-wide mobile homes/trailers

1. Gather the required documentation

You will need to obtain the following documents before submitting your request:

  • The Original Certificate of Title
  • A description of the home, including;
    • Model Year
    • Manufacturer {make}
    • Width
    • Length
    • Identification Number/Serial Number
  • Lien Release Documentation, if applicable
  • The legal description of the real property
  • A sworn statement confirming:
    • You own both the land, and the Tiny Home or Manufactured Home, or a sworn statement from the property land owner
    • The home is permanently affixed to the property/ground

If you are unable to locate your current Certificate of Title for Tiny Home or Manufactured Home, you are able to request a duplicate title by printing off the Duplicate Title Request Application {MVT-8} and mailing it into our Bureau of Motor Vehicles office with a $33 check-or-moneyorder payable to "Secretary of State". Once a duplicate title is obtained, you wll then be able to continue to the next step.
2. Record the appropriate documents with the Registry of Deeds

Take all the above documents listed to the Registry of Deeds in the county where the property is located. The Registry of Deeds will record the documents as part of the public land records.

For further information on the nearest Registry of Deeds and other contact information, please Maine Registry of Deeds 

3. Submit the Request for Cancellation of Certificate of Title

After the documents above have been recorded, submit a completed MVT-51: Request for Cancellation of Certificate of Title for Tiny Home or Manufactured Housing and provide all original documentation that was recorded within the Registry of Deeds {photocopies are not accepted}. Be sure to include the Book and Page number from the prior step from the Registry of Deeds

4. Receive Confirmation and record Cancellation Letter with Registry of Deeds

Once the Secretary of State reviews and approves your request, you will be mailed a Cancellation Letter stating the process is complete. You must then have the Cancellation Letter document recorded within the county Registry of Deeds. This is a crucial step, as the application process is pending the verification of receipt and recording at the Registry of Deeds office.

5. Return proof of recording to the Bureau of Motor Vehicles

As mentioned above, this process is dependent on the documentation within the public record of the residential real property. Once that document has been recorded within the Registry of Deeds, please return proof of filing with the Bureau of Motor Vehicles via email, both of which are listed below;

Email: titles.bmv@maine.gov

Disclaimer: This information is intended as a general overview of the Maine titling process for Tiny Homes and Manufactured Homes. Requirements may vary depending on the circumstances of the transaction. For further information, please contact the Title Services Division at 207-624-9000 extension 52138, Monday through Friday 08:30AM to 4:30PM
